Let \(t=2^p\). In \(KG(7,2)\), two distinct \(2\)-subsets are either disjoint or meet in one point, so

\[
d(A,B)=
\begin{cases}
0,&A=B,\\
1,&A\cap B=\varnothing,\\
2,&A\cap B\neq\varnothing,\ A\neq B.
\end{cases}
\]

Let \(A\) be the adjacency matrix of \(KG(7,2)\), and let \(J\) be the all-ones matrix. On the zero-sum subspace, \(J=0\), and

\[
D_p=(d(A,B)^p)=(1-t)A-tI.
\]

The adjacency operator has eigenvalues on \(\mathbb R^{\binom{[7]}2}\):

\[
10,\qquad -4,\qquad 1
\]

with multiplicities \(1,6,14\). Indeed, the \(-4\)-eigenspace consists of vectors

\[
c_{\{i,j\}}=x_i+x_j,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^7 x_i=0,
\]

and has dimension \(6\).

Thus on the zero-sum subspace the eigenvalues of \(D_p\) are

\[
(1-t)(-4)-t=3t-4
\]

on the \(6\)-dimensional space above, and

\[
(1-t)(1)-t=1-2t
\]

on the remaining \(14\)-dimensional space. Negative type requires both to be \(\le 0\). Since \(p>0\), \(t>1\), so \(1-2t<0\). The critical condition is

\[
3t-4\le 0,
\]

hence

\[
2^p\le \frac43.
\]

Therefore

\[
\wp=\log_2\frac43.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), the nullspace \(E\) is exactly

\[
E=\left\{c_{\{i,j\}}=x_i+x_j:\sum_{i=1}^7x_i=0\right\},
\]

so

\[
\dim E=6.
\]

Now identify \(E\) with the \(6\)-dimensional space

\[
H=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^7:\sum_i x_i=0\right\}.
\]

For a subspace \(U\le H\), the edge \(\{i,j\}\) is absent from the support exactly when

\[
x_i+x_j=0
\]

for every \(x\in U\). Thus minimizing support is the same as maximizing the number of pair constraints \(x_i+x_j=0\) that hold on an \(r\)-dimensional subspace.

Such constraints form a graph on \([7]\). In each connected bipartite component, the variables are determined by one parameter, with opposite signs on the two parts. In each non-bipartite component, all variables are forced to be \(0\). The global condition \(\sum_i x_i=0\) removes one dimension unless every bipartite component is balanced.

A finite optimization over component types gives the maximum possible number \(M_r\) of vanished pairs:

\[
(M_1,M_2,M_3,M_4,M_5,M_6)=(11,6,4,2,1,0).
\]

These bounds are attained as follows:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
r & \text{vanishing-edge pattern}\\
\hline
1 & K_5\cup K_{1,1}\\
2 & K_4\cup 3\text{ isolated vertices}\\
3 & K_{2,2}\cup 3\text{ isolated vertices}\\
4 & K_{1,1}\cup K_{1,1}\cup 3\text{ isolated vertices}\\
5 & K_{1,1}\cup 5\text{ isolated vertices}\\
6 & \text{empty graph}
\end{array}
\]

Since \(|X|=\binom72=21\),

\[
d_r=21-M_r.
\]

Therefore

\[
(d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4,d_5,d_6)
=
(10,15,17,19,20,21).
\]

Final answer:

\[
\boxed{\left(\log_2\frac43,\ 6,\ (10,15,17,19,20,21)\right)}.
\]
